text: In a Vernier calipers, when both jaws touch each other, zero of the Vernier scale is shifted to the right of zero of the main scale and $7^{\text{th}}$ Vernier division coincides with a main scale reading. If the value of 1 main scale division is 1 mm and there are 10 Vernier scale divisions, then the Vernier caliper has
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 5th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The Least Count is the smallest measurement that can be accurately taken using the instrument.

For a Vernier calliper, the difference between the length of one Main Scale Division (MSD) and one Vernier Scale Division (VSD) is equal to the least count.

$\mathrm{LC}=1\mathrm{MSD}-1\mathrm{VSD}$

It is given that $1\mathrm{MSD}=1\mathrm{mm}$.

In a standard Vernier calliper arrangement, 10 divisions on the Vernier scale correspond to the length of 9 divisions on the Main scale.

$10\mathrm{VSD}=9\mathrm{MSD}$

$\Rightarrow$ $1\mathrm{VSD}=\frac{9}{10}\mathrm{MSD}=0.9\mathrm{mm}$

So, the least count is;

$\mathrm{LC}=1\mathrm{mm}-0.9\mathrm{mm}=0.1\mathrm{mm}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{LC}=0.1\mathrm{mm}=0.01\mathrm{cm}$

Zero error occurs when the jaws of the calliper are completely closed but the zero mark of the main scale does not align with the zero mark of the Vernier scale.

If the zero of the Vernier scale rests to the right of the main scale zero, the instrument will naturally measure a value larger than the true length and this is positive zero error.

If the zero of the Vernier scale rests to the left of the main scale zero, it creates a negative zero error.

It is given that the zero of the Vernier scale is shifted to the right. Therefore, the given Vernier scale is with a positive zero error.

If Vernier division perfectly coincides with any main scale reading, then the zero error is,

$\mathrm{e}=\mathrm{n}\times \mathrm{LC}$

Where n is the coinciding division. The problem states that the $7^{\text{th}}$ division coincides.

$\mathrm{e}=7\times 0.01\mathrm{cm}=0.07\mathrm{cm}$

Since the shift is to the right, the final error is +0.07 cm . 

Thus, the correct option is (C).

text: $L,C$ and $R$ represents physical quantities inductance, capacitance and resistance respectively. The dimensional formula $\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-4}\mathrm{A}^{-2}$ corresponds to $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 5th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From $P=I^{2}R$, with $[P]=[\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-3}]$:

$[R]=\dfrac{[\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-3}]}{[\mathrm{A}^{2}]}=[\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-3}\mathrm{A}^{-2}]$

The time constants $τ=\dfrac{L}{R}$ and $τ=RC$ give $[L]=[R][\mathrm{T}]$ and $[C]=\dfrac{[\mathrm{T}]}{[R]}$, so $[LC]=[\mathrm{T}^{2}]$ and $\left [\dfrac{L}{C}\right ]=[R]^{2}$.

(A) $\left [\dfrac{R}{\sqrt{LC}}\right ]=\dfrac{[\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-3}\mathrm{A}^{-2}]}{[\mathrm{T}]}=[\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-4}\mathrm{A}^{-2}]$, which matches.

(B) $\left [\dfrac{R}{LC}\right ]=\dfrac{[R]}{[\mathrm{T}^{2}]}=[\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-5}\mathrm{A}^{-2}]$.

(C) $\left [\dfrac{C}{\sqrt{LR}}\right ]=\dfrac{[\mathrm{T}]/[R]}{[R][\mathrm{T}]^{1/2}}=\dfrac{[\mathrm{T}]^{1/2}}{[R]^{2}}=[\mathrm{M}^{-2}\mathrm{L}^{-4}\mathrm{T}^{13/2}\mathrm{A}^{4}]$.

(D) $\left [\dfrac{1}{R}\sqrt{\dfrac{L}{C}}\right ]=\dfrac{[R]}{[R]}=[\mathrm{M}^{0}\mathrm{L}^{0}\mathrm{T}^{0}]$, dimensionless.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
When one moves from a point 16 km below the earth's surface to a point 16 km above the earth's surface, the change in g is approximately $α%$. The value of $α$ is $____$ .

(Take radius of the earth $=6400\mathrm{km}$.)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 5th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The acceleration due to gravity at a depth d below the Earth's surface is given by the formula :

$\mathrm{g}_{\mathrm{d}}=\mathrm{g}\left (1-\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{R}}\right )$

Where $g$ is the acceleration at the surface, $d$ is the depth, and $R$ is the radius of the Earth.

The depth is given as $\mathrm{d}=16\mathrm{km}$ and $\mathrm{R}=6400\mathrm{km}$ :

$g_{d}=g\left (1-\frac{16}{6400}\right )$

The acceleration due to gravity at a height $h$ above the Earth's surface (for $h\ll R$ ) is given by the approximation :

$g_{h}=g\left (1-\frac{2h}{R}\right )$

Where h is the height above the surface.

The height is given as $\mathrm{h}=16\mathrm{km}$ and $\mathrm{R}=6400\mathrm{km}$ :

$g_{h}=g\left (1-\frac{2\times 16}{6400}\right )=g\left (1-\frac{32}{6400}\right )$

The change in $g$ as we move from depth to height is :

$\Delta \mathrm{g}=\mathrm{g}_{\mathrm{h}}-\mathrm{g}_{\mathrm{d}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta g=g\left (1-\frac{32}{6400}\right )-g\left (1-\frac{16}{6400}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta g=g\left (1-\frac{32}{6400}-1+\frac{16}{6400}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta g=g\left (-\frac{16}{6400}\right )$

The magnitude of the change is $|\Delta \mathrm{g}|=\mathrm{g}\left (\frac{16}{6400}\right )=\mathrm{g}\left (\frac{1}{400}\right )$.

So, the percentage change is,

$α=\left (\frac{|\Delta \mathrm{g}|}{\mathrm{g}}\right )\times 100$

$\Rightarrow$ $α=\left (\frac{1}{400}\right )\times 100=\frac{1}{4}=0.25$

Therefore, the correct option is (B).

Three masses $m_{1}=4\mathrm{kg},m_{2}=4\mathrm{kg}$ and $m_{3}=6\mathrm{kg}$ are suspended from a fixed smooth frictionless pulley as shown in the figure below. The value of $T_{1}/T_{2}$ is

$____$

(take $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$ )

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 5th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The masses $\mathrm{m}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{m}_{2}$ are on one side of the pulley, and $\mathrm{m}_{3}$ is on the other.

Total mass on right side is $\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{R}}=\mathrm{m}_{2}+\mathrm{m}_{3}=4+6=10\mathrm{kg}$.

Total mass on left side is $\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{L}}=\mathrm{m}_{1}=4\mathrm{kg}$.


[IMG]


Since $M_{L}<M_{R}$, the system will accelerate toward the right side. Let the acceleration be $a$.

For right side, $\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{R}}\mathrm{g}-\mathrm{T}_{1}=\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{R}}\mathrm{a}\Rightarrow 10\mathrm{g}-\mathrm{T}_{1}=10\mathrm{a}$

For left side, $\mathrm{T}_{1}-\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{L}}\mathrm{g}=\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{L}}\mathrm{a}\Rightarrow \mathrm{T}_{1}-4\mathrm{g}=4\mathrm{a}\ldots$

From both the equations,

$\mathrm{T}_{1}-4\mathrm{g}=4\left (\frac{10\mathrm{g}-\mathrm{T}_{1}}{10}\right )\Rightarrow \frac{10}{4}(\mathrm{T}_{1}-40)=100-\mathrm{T}_{1}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{5\mathrm{T}_{1}}{2}-100=100-\mathrm{T}_{1}\Rightarrow \frac{5\mathrm{T}_{1}}{2}+\mathrm{T}_{1}=200$

$\Rightarrow \frac{7\mathrm{T}_{1}}{2}=200\Rightarrow \mathrm{T}_{1}=\frac{400}{7}\mathrm{N}\ldots (ii)$

Putting in equation (ii), we get the acceleration of the system;

$\mathrm{a}=\frac{\mathrm{T}_{1}-4\mathrm{g}}{4}=\frac{\frac{400}{7}-40}{4}=\frac{120}{7\times 4}=\frac{30}{7}\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}\ldots (iv)$

The acceleration of whole system is $30/7\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$,

For mass $\mathrm{m}_{3}$;


[IMG]


$\mathrm{m}_{3}\mathrm{g}-\mathrm{T}_{2}=\mathrm{m}_{3}\mathrm{a}\Rightarrow \mathrm{T}_{2}=\mathrm{m}_{3}(\mathrm{g}-\mathrm{a})$

$\mathrm{T}_{2}=6\left (10-\frac{30}{7}\right )\mathrm{N}=6\times \frac{40}{7}=\frac{240}{7}\ldots (\mathrm{v})$

So, the ratio is $\frac{\mathrm{T}_{1}}{\mathrm{T}_{2}}$ is;

$\frac{\mathrm{T}_{1}}{\mathrm{T}_{2}}=\frac{400/7}{240/7}=\frac{400}{240}=\frac{5}{3}$

Therefore, the correct option is (A).

text:
A wedge $Y$ with mass of 10 kg and all frictionless surfaces and the inclined surface making $37^{\circ }$ with horizontal. A block $X$ with mass 2 kg is placed at the highest point of the wedge as shown in figure is at rest. At $t=0$ wedge ( $Y$ ) is pulled toward right with constant force $(f)$ of 24 N . Taking the block $X$ at rest at $t=0$, the time taken by it to slide down 8.8 m on the slope, while $Y$ is on the move, is $____$ s.

$(~$ take $\tan (37^{\circ })=3/4$ and $\left. \mathrm{g}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}\right )$

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 5th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the acceleration of wedge along horizontal is $\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{w}}$ and whole system will accelerate to the right.


[IMG]


Total mass of the system is $\mathrm{M}=\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{X}}+\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{Y}}=(10+2)\mathrm{kg}=12\mathrm{kg}$

The applied force along horizontal is $\mathrm{f}=24\mathrm{N}$

Using Newton's second law of motion for the system, acceleration of wedge,

$\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{w}}=\frac{\mathrm{f}}{\mathrm{M}}=\frac{24}{12}=2\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$

The block X will be at rest along normal to the incline when motion is observed with respect to wedge Y . So, in the non-inertial frame of the wedge, a pseudo-force $(\mathrm{ma}_{\mathrm{w}})$ acts on block X toward the left. Components of forces acting along the incline for block X :


[IMG]


Component of gravity is $\mathrm{mg}\sin (37^{\circ })$ (down the incline).

Component of pseudo-force is $\mathrm{ma}_{\mathrm{w}}\cos (37^{\circ })$ (up the incline)

So, the acceleration of block X down the incline relative to wedge is;

$a_{\mathrm{X}}=g\sin (37^{\circ })-a_{\mathrm{w}}\cos (37^{\circ })$

$\Rightarrow$ $a_{\mathrm{X}}=(10)\left (\frac{3}{5}\right )-(2)\left (\frac{4}{5}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{x}}=6-1.6=4.4\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$

Distance to slide along the incline is $\mathrm{s}=8.8\mathrm{m}$.

Initial relative velocity of block X is $\mathrm{u}=0$.

Using equation of motion;

$\mathrm{s}=\mathrm{ut}+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{X}}\mathrm{t}^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $8.8=0+\frac{1}{2}(4.4)\mathrm{t}^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{t}^{2}=\frac{8.8\times 2}{4.4}$

$\Rightarrow$ $t^{2}=4\Rightarrow t=2s$

Therefore, the block X will take 2 s to slide 8.8 m down the incline of wedge Y . 

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
The Young's modulus of steel wire of radius $r$ and length $L$ is $Y$.

If the radius $r$ and length $L$ of the wire are doubled then the value of $Y$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 5th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Young's Modulus is defined as the ratio of tensile stress $(σ)$ to tensile strain $(𝜖)$ :

$\mathrm{Y}=\frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}}=\frac{\mathrm{F}/\mathrm{A}}{\Delta \mathrm{L}/\mathrm{L}}$

Young's Modulus is an intrinsic property of the material. It depends solely on the nature of the material and the temperature, not on the dimensions (length, area, or radius) of the specific sample.

The radius ( r ) and length ( L ) are doubled.

Doubling the radius changes the area $\left (A=πr^{2}\right )$, the area of cross-section becomes 4 times the initial and doubling the length changes the original length (L).

However, because the material remains steel, the inter-atomic forces and the elastic constant of the substance do not change.

Since Young's modulus (Y) is independent of dimensions, changing $L$ or $r$ will not affect the value of Y.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason $𝐑$

Statement I : Change in internal energy of a system containing $n$ mole of ideal gas can be written as $\Delta \mathrm{U}=n\mathrm{C}_{v}(T_{\mathrm{f}}-T_{i})=\frac{nR}{γ-1}(T_{\mathrm{f}}-T_{i})$, where $γ=\frac{C_{p}}{C_{v}},T_{i}=$ initial temperature, $T_{\mathrm{f}}=$ final temperature.

Statement II : Relation between degree of freedom $f$ and $γ(=C_{p}/C_{v})$ is $\left (γ=1+\frac{2}{f}\right )$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both $𝐀$ and $𝐑$ are true and $𝐑$ is the correct explanation of $𝐀$
Both $𝐀$ and $𝐑$ are true but $𝐑$ is NOT the correct explanation of $𝐀$
A is true but $𝐑$ is false
A is false but $𝐑$ is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 5th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Internal energy ( $U$ ) of an ideal gas depends only on temperature. The change in internal energy for any process is given by:

$\Delta \mathrm{U}=\mathrm{nC}_{\mathrm{v}}\Delta \mathrm{T}=\mathrm{nC}_{\mathrm{v}}(\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{f}}-\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{i}})$

According to Mayer's relation, $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{p}}-\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{v}}=\mathrm{R}$.

$\frac{C_{p}}{C_{v}}-1=\frac{R}{C_{v}}$

Since $γ=\frac{\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{v}}}$, then $γ-1=\frac{\mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{v}}}\Rightarrow \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{v}}=\frac{\mathrm{R}}{γ-1}$.

Substituting $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{v}}$ back into the $\Delta \mathrm{U}$ equation:

$\Delta \mathrm{U}=\frac{\mathrm{nR}}{γ-1}(\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{f}}-\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{i}})$

Thus, Statement I is true.

From the law of equipartition of energy, the molar specific heat at constant volume is $C_{v}=\frac{f}{2}R$, where $f$ is the degree of freedom.

Using $C_{p}=C_{v}+R=\frac{f}{2}R+R=R\left (1+\frac{f}{2}\right )$.

The ratio $γ=\frac{\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{v}}}=\frac{\mathrm{R}\left (1+\frac{\mathrm{f}}{2}\right )}{(\mathrm{f}/2)\mathrm{R}}=\frac{1+\mathrm{f}/2}{\mathrm{f}/2}=\frac{2}{\mathrm{f}}+1$.

So, $γ=1+2$ f.

Thus, Statement II is true.

Statement II is the definition of $γ$ in terms of degrees of freedom, but Statement I is based on Mayer's relation which is the definition of $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{v}}$, i.e., not directly from the degrees of freedom.

Therefore, both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A . 

Thus, the correct option is (B).

text:
Consider the following statements:

A. Zeroth law of thermodynamics gives concept of temperature

B. First law of thermodynamics gives concept of internal energy

C. In isothermal expansion of ideal gas, $\Delta Q\neq \Delta W$

D. Product of intensive and extensive variables is extensive

E. The ratio of any extensive variable to mass will be an extensive variable

Choose the correct combination of statements from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 5th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The Zeroth Law states that if two systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third system, they are in thermal equilibrium with each other, i.e., the Zeroth law gives idea about the property of temperature to be measured. Hence, statement A is true.

The First Law is the mathematical relation between heat ( $\Delta \mathrm{Q}$ ), change in internal energy ( $\Delta \mathrm{U}$ ) and work done by the system ( $\Delta \mathrm{W}$ )

$\Delta \mathrm{Q}=\Delta \mathrm{U}+\Delta \mathrm{W}$

This relation introduces internal energy ( $U$ ) as a state function which is based on energy conservation. Hence, statement B is true.

In an isothermal expansion of an ideal gas, temperature remains constant, so $\Delta U=0$.

From the First Law: $\Delta \mathrm{Q}=\Delta \mathrm{U}+\Delta \mathrm{W}\Rightarrow \Delta \mathrm{Q}=0+\Delta \mathrm{W}\Rightarrow \Delta \mathrm{Q}=\Delta \mathrm{W}$.

But as per statement $C$, in isothermal process $\Delta Q\neq \Delta W$, so statement $C$ is False.

Intensive variables are the properties which do not depend on size, for example temperature and pressure.

Extensive variables are the properties depend on size, for example volume.

The product of intensive and extensive property $\mathrm{P}\times \mathrm{V}$ represents work or energy, which depends with the size of the system. Therefore, the product is extensive.

When an extensive variable (like volume or heat capacity) is divided by mass, it becomes a specific quantity (like specific volume or specific heat). Specific quantities are intensive because they do not depend on the total mass of the system. Statement E says it remains extensive, so it is False.

Therefore, only A, B, and D are correct. Hence, the correct option is (C).

solution.body:
[IMG]


Using Kirchhoff's current law, the net accumulation of current at a junction is zero.

So, at junction $\mathrm{A},\mathrm{I}_{1}-\mathrm{I}_{3}-\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{AD}}=0\Rightarrow \mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{AD}}=\mathrm{I}_{1}-\mathrm{I}_{3}$

And at junction $\mathrm{D},\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{AD}}+\mathrm{I}_{2}-\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{DB}}=0\Rightarrow \mathrm{I}_{1}-\mathrm{I}_{3}+\mathrm{I}_{2}-\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{DB}}=0\Rightarrow \mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{DB}}=\mathrm{I}_{1}-\mathrm{I}_{3}+\mathrm{I}_{2}$

Applying Kirchhoff's voltage law in closed loop I,

$-4(\mathrm{I}_{1}-\mathrm{I}_{3})-2(\mathrm{I}_{1}+\mathrm{I}_{2}-\mathrm{I}_{3})-\mathrm{I}_{1}+10=0$

$-7\mathrm{I}_{1}-2\mathrm{I}_{2}+6\mathrm{I}_{3}=-10\ldots (i)$

In loop (II)

$-I_{1}+10-4I_{3}-2(I_{3}-I_{2})=0$

$2\mathrm{I}_{2}-6\mathrm{I}_{3}-\mathrm{I}_{1}=-10\ldots \text{(ii)}$

In loop III,

$-5-2(\mathrm{I}_{3}-\mathrm{I}_{2})+2(\mathrm{I}_{1}+\mathrm{I}_{2}-\mathrm{I}_{3})=0$

$2\mathrm{I}_{1}+4\mathrm{I}_{2}-4\mathrm{I}_{3}=5.....(iii)$

From equation (iii),

$I_{1}=\frac{5-4I_{2}+4I_{3}}{2}\ldots (iv)$

On substituting equation (iv) in equation (ii);

$2\mathrm{I}_{2}-6\mathrm{I}_{3}-\frac{5-4\mathrm{I}_{2}+4\mathrm{I}_{3}}{2}=-10$

$\Rightarrow 4\mathrm{I}_{2}-12\mathrm{I}_{3}-5+4\mathrm{I}_{2}-4\mathrm{I}_{3}=-20$

$\Rightarrow 8\mathrm{I}_{2}-16\mathrm{I}_{3}=-15$

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{I}_{2}-2\mathrm{I}_{3}=-\frac{15}{8}$

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{I}_{2}=2\mathrm{I}_{3}-\frac{15}{8}\ldots (\mathrm{v})$

On substituting equation (v) in equation (iv),

$\mathrm{I}_{1}=\frac{5-4\left (2\mathrm{I}_{3}-\frac{15}{8}\right )}{2}=\frac{5-8\mathrm{I}_{3}+\frac{15}{2}+4\mathrm{I}_{3}}{2}=\frac{\frac{25}{2}-4\mathrm{I}_{3}}{2}=\frac{25}{4}-2\mathrm{I}_{3}$

$\Rightarrow$ $I_{1}=\dfrac{25}{4}-2I_{3}\ldots (vi)$

Substituting equation (v) and (vi) in equation (i);

$-7\left (\frac{25}{4}-2\mathrm{I}_{3}\right )-2\left (2\mathrm{I}_{3}-\frac{15}{8}\right )+6\mathrm{I}_{3}=-10$

$\begin{array}{l} -\dfrac{175}{4}+14\mathrm{I}_{3}-4\mathrm{I}_{3}+\dfrac{15}{4}+6\mathrm{I}_{3}=-10 \\ \dfrac{-175+15}{4}+16\mathrm{I}_{3}=-10 \\ \dfrac{-160}{4}+16\mathrm{I}_{3}=-10 \\ -40+16\mathrm{I}_{3}=-10 \\ 16\mathrm{I}_{3}=30\Rightarrow \mathrm{I}_{3}=\dfrac{30}{16}\mathrm{A} \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{I}_{3}=1.875\mathrm{A} \end{array}$

From equation (v)

$I_{2}=2\left (\frac{15}{8}\right )-\frac{15}{8}=\frac{15}{8}=1.875\mathrm{A}$

From equation (vi),

$I_{1}=\frac{25}{4}-2\left (\frac{15}{8}\right )=\frac{25}{4}-\frac{15}{4}=\frac{10}{4}\mathrm{A}=2.5\mathrm{A}$

Therefore, the values of currents in the circuit are; $\mathrm{I}_{1}=2.5\mathrm{A},\mathrm{I}_{2}=1.875\mathrm{A},\mathrm{I}_{3}=1.875\mathrm{A}$. 

Thus, the correct option is (A).

text:
An electron of mass $m$ is moving in an electric field $⃗{E}=-2E_{\mathrm{o}}\hat{i}(E_{\mathrm{o}}=$ constant $>0)$, with an initial velocity $⃗{V}=v_{\mathrm{o}}\hat{i}(v_{\mathrm{o}}=$ constant $>0)$. If $λ_{\mathrm{o}}=\frac{h}{4mv_{\mathrm{o}}}$, its de Broglie wavelength at time $t$ is

$____$ .

( $e=$ charge of electron)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 5th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The force on an electron (charge -e) in an electric field $\vec{\mathrm{E}}$ is $\vec{\mathrm{F}}=-\mathrm{e}\vec{\mathrm{E}}$.

The electric field is given $\vec{\mathrm{E}}=-2\mathrm{E}_{0}\hat{\mathrm{i}}$,

So, the force acting on electron is,

$\vec{\mathrm{F}}=(-\mathrm{e})\left (-2\mathrm{E}_{0}\hat{\mathrm{i}}\right )=2\mathrm{eE}_{0}\hat{\mathrm{i}}$

Using Newton's second law of motion, $\vec{\mathrm{F}}=\mathrm{m}\vec{\mathrm{a}}$ the acceleration of electron is;

$\vec{\mathrm{a}}=\frac{\vec{\mathrm{F}}}{\mathrm{m}}=\frac{2\mathrm{eE}_{0}}{\mathrm{m}}\hat{\mathrm{i}}$

Using the first equation of motion ( $⃗{v}=⃗{u}+⃗{a}t$ ), the final velocity of electron at any time $t$ is;

$\vec{\mathrm{v}}(\mathrm{t})=\mathrm{v}_{0}+\left (\frac{2\mathrm{eE}_{0}}{\mathrm{m}}\right )\mathrm{t}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{\mathrm{v}}(\mathrm{t})=\mathrm{v}_{0}\left (1+\frac{2\mathrm{eE}_{0}\mathrm{t}}{\mathrm{mv}_{0}}\right )$

The de Broglie wavelength is $λ=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{p}}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{mv}}$.

Substituting the velocity:

$λ_{t}=\frac{h}{mv_{0}\left (1+\frac{2eE0t}{mv0}\right )}$

It is given that $λ_{0}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{4\mathrm{mv}_{0}}\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{mv}_{0}}=4λ_{0}$.

$λ_{t}=\frac{4λ_{0}}{1+\frac{2\mathrm{eE}0t}{\mathrm{mv}0}}$

Therefore, the correct option is (C).

text:
In the hydrogen atom, the electron makes a transition from the higher orbit (i) to a lower orbit $(f)$. The ratio of the radius of the orbits in given by $r_{i}:r_{f}=16:4$. The wavelength of photon emitted due to this transition is $____$ nm.

(Given Rydberg constant $=1.0973\times 10^{7}/\mathrm{m}$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 5th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The radius of an electron in the $\mathrm{n}^{\text{th}}$ orbit of a hydrogen atom is given by the formula:

$r_{n}=\left (\frac{𝜖_{0}h^{2}}{πme^{2}}\right )n^{2}\Rightarrow r_{n}\propto n^{2}$

The ratio of radii of $i^{\text{th}}$ orbit to $f^{\text{th}}$ orbit is $r_{i}:r_{f}=16:4$,

$\frac{\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{i}}^{2}}{\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{f}}^{2}}=\frac{16}{4}=4$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{i}}}{\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{f}}}=2\Rightarrow \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{i}}=2\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{f}}$

For a transition to a lower orbit in a hydrogen atom, the simplest integers satisfying this are $\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{f}}=2$ and $\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{i}}=$ 4.

The wavelength of the emitted photon is given by the Rydberg formula:

$\frac{1}{λ}=\mathrm{R}\left (\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{f}}^{2}}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{i}}^{2}}\right )$

Substituting the values $\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{f}}=2$ and $\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{i}}=4$ :

$\frac{1}{λ}=\mathrm{R}\left (\frac{1}{2^{2}}-\frac{1}{4^{2}}\right )=\mathrm{R}\left (\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{16}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{λ}=\mathrm{R}\left (\frac{4-1}{16}\right )=\frac{3\mathrm{R}}{16}$

$\Rightarrow$ $λ=\frac{16}{3R}$

Putting the value of Rydberg's constant $\mathrm{R}=1.0973\times 10^{7}\mathrm{m}^{-1}$

$λ=\frac{16}{3\times 1.0973\times 10^{7}}\approx 4.86\times 10^{-7}\mathrm{m}=486\times 10^{-9}\mathrm{m}$

$\Rightarrow$ $λ=486\mathrm{nm}$

Therefore, the wavelength of photon emitted due to this transition is 486 nm . 

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: A displacement current of 4.0 A can be set up in the space between two parallel plates of $6μ\mathrm{F}$ capacitor. The rate of change of potential difference across the plates of the capacitor is nearly $α\times 10^{6}\mathrm{V}/\mathrm{s}$. The value of $α$ is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 5th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
According to Maxwell's law, the displacement current in a capacitor is equal to the rate of change of charge on the plates $\left (\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{d}}=\frac{\mathrm{d}\mathrm{Q}}{\mathrm{dt}}\right )$.

The charge ( $Q$ ) on a capacitor of capacitance ( $C$ ), connected to potential difference (V) is:

$Q=CV$

On differentiating both sides with respect to time $(t)$ :

$\frac{dQ}{dt}=C\frac{dV}{dt}$

Since displacement current is $I_{d}=\frac{dQ}{dt}$, we have:

$I_{d}=C\frac{dV}{dt}$

The displacement current is given as $\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{d}}=4.0\mathrm{A}$ and the capacitance of capacitor is $\mathrm{C}=6μ\mathrm{F}=6\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{F}$ : Putting the values,

$\frac{\mathrm{dV}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{d}}}{\mathrm{C}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{dV}{dt}=\frac{4.0}{6\times 10^{-6}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\mathrm{dV}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{2}{3}\times 10^{6}\approx 0.67\times 10^{6}\frac{\mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{s}}=α\times 10^{6}\frac{\mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{s}}$

$\Rightarrow α=0.67$

Therefore, the correct option is (B).

text: In Young's double slit experiment, the fringe width of the interference pattern produced on the screen is $2.4μ\mathrm{m}$. If the experiment is carried out in another medium having refractive index 1.2 , the fringe width will be $____$ $μ\mathrm{m}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 5th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In Young's Double Slit Experiment (YDSE), the fringe width ( $β$ ) is given by :

$β=\frac{λD}{d}$

Where, $λ$ is the wavelength of light used, D is the distance between the slits and the screen, and d is the distance between the two slits.

When the experiment is moved from air/vacuum to a medium with a refractive index $μ$, the speed of light decreases, which in turn decreases the wavelength. The new wavelength $λ^{'}$ is:

$λ^{'}=\frac{λ}{μ}$

Since D and d are constant for the experimental setup, the new fringe width $β^{'}$ in the medium is :

$β^{'}=\frac{λ^{'}D}{d}=\frac{\left (\frac{λ}{μ}\right )D}{d}=\frac{1}{μ}\left (\frac{λD}{d}\right )$

Therefore $β^{'}=\frac{β}{μ}$

The original fringe width (when setup is in air) is $β=2.4μ\mathrm{m}$.

The refractive index of the medium is $μ=1.2$.

Putting the values,

$β^{'}=\frac{2.4}{1.2}=2.0μ\mathrm{m}$

Therefore, the correct option is (B).

text:
A ray of light passing through an equilateral prism is having velocity $2.12\times 10^{8}\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ in the prism material, then the minimum angle of deviation is

$____$ degrees.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 5th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The refractive index is the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum (c) to the speed of light in the medium (v).

$μ=\frac{c}{v}$

The speed of light in vacuum is $\mathrm{c}=3\times 10^{8}\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ and the speed of light in material of prism is given as $\mathrm{v}=2.12\times 10^{8}\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$.

So, the refractive index of material of prism is;

$μ=\frac{3\times 10^{8}}{2.12\times 10^{8}}\approx 1.414\approx \sqrt{2}$

As the prism is equilateral, so the angle of prism is $\mathrm{A}=60^{\circ }$.

The the angle of minimum deviation through prism is given as,

$μ=\frac{\sin \left (\frac{A+δm}{2}\right )}{\sin \left (\frac{A}{2}\right )}$

Substituting the refractive index $μ=\sqrt{2}$ and prism angle $\mathrm{A}=60^{\circ }$ :

$\sqrt{2}=\frac{\sin \left (\frac{60+δ\mathrm{m}}{2}\right )}{\sin \left (\frac{60}{2}\right )}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\sqrt{2}=\frac{\sin \left (\frac{60+δm}{2}\right )}{\sin (30^{\circ })}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\sqrt{2}\times 0.5=\sin \left (\frac{60+δ_{m}}{2}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}=\sin \left (\frac{60+δ_{m}}{2}\right )\Rightarrow \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\sin \left (\frac{60+δ_{m}}{2}\right )=\sin 45^{\circ }$

$\Rightarrow$ $45^{\circ }=\frac{60+δ_{\mathrm{m}}}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $90^{\circ }=60^{\circ }+δ_{\mathrm{m}}\Rightarrow δ_{\mathrm{m}}=30^{\circ }$

Therefore, the correct option is (B).

text:
Light source having wavelength 331 nm is used to generate photo-electrons whose stopping potential is 0.2 V . The work function of the used metal in the experiment is $α\times 10^{-19}\mathrm{J}$. The value of $α$ is $____$ .

$\left (\mathrm{h}=6.62\times 10^{-34}\mathrm{J}\mathrm{s},\mathrm{e}=1.6\times 10^{-19}\mathrm{C}\text{and}\mathrm{c}=3\times 10^{8}\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}\right )$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 5th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
If the energy of an incident photon is $E$ then it is equal to the energy required to overcome the work function $(𝜙)$ of the metal and the maximum kinetic energy ( $\mathrm{K}_{\max }$ ) to the emitted electron.

$\mathrm{E}=𝜙+\mathrm{K}_{\max }$

Therefore, $𝜙=\mathrm{E}-\mathrm{K}_{\max }$.

Energy is given by $\mathrm{E}=\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{λ}$ where the Planck's constant $\mathrm{h}=6.62\times 10^{-34}\mathrm{J}\mathrm{s}$, the speed of light $\mathrm{c}=3\times 10^{8}\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$, and the wavelength of light is $λ=331\mathrm{nm}=331\times 10^{-9}\mathrm{m}$ :

Putting the values,

$E=\frac{\left (6.62\times 10^{-34}\right )\times \left (3\times 10^{8}\right )}{331\times 10^{-9}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $E=\frac{19.86\times 10^{-26}}{331\times 10^{-9}}=\frac{1986\times 10^{-28}}{331\times 10^{-9}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{E}=6\times 10^{-19}\mathrm{J}$

The maximum kinetic energy is related to the stopping potential ( $\mathrm{V}_{0}$ ) by:

$\mathrm{K}_{\max }=\mathrm{e}\mathrm{V}_{0}$

The electronic charge is $\mathrm{e}=1.6\times 10^{-19}\mathrm{C}$ and the stopping potential is $\mathrm{V}_{0}=0.2\mathrm{V}$ :

$\mathrm{K}_{\max }=\left (1.6\times 10^{-19}\right )\times 0.2=0.32\times 10^{-19}\mathrm{J}$

So, the work function of metal is,

$𝜙=\mathrm{E}-\mathrm{K}_{\max }$

$\Rightarrow$ $𝜙=\left (6\times 10^{-19}\right )-\left (0.32\times 10^{-19}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $𝜙=5.68\times 10^{-19}\mathrm{J}=α\times 10^{-19}\mathrm{J}\Rightarrow α=5.68$

Therefore, the correct option is (C).

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 5th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
According to the lens maker's formula, the focal length (f) of a symmetric biconvex lens with radius of curvature R and refractive index $μ$ is :


[IMG]


$\frac{1}{f}=(μ-1)\left (\frac{1}{R}-\frac{1}{-R}\right )=\frac{2(μ-1)}{R}$

When the lens is cut vertically, the new lens is plano-convex with one flat surface ( $\mathrm{R}_{2}=\infty$ ). Its focal length $(f^{'})$ is :

Where L is the tube length, $\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{o}}$ is the focal length of the objective, and $\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{e}}$ is the focal length of the eyepiece.

$M=\frac{L}{f_{o}}=\frac{L^{'}}{2f_{o}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{L}^{'}=2\mathrm{L}$

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 5th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Breaking tension ( $\mathrm{T}_{\max }$ ) is the maximum tension that can wire withstand without breaking.

If the breaking stress of wire is $σ_{\max }$ and area of cross-section is $\mathrm{A},σ_{\max }=\frac{\mathrm{T}_{\max }}{\mathrm{A}}\Rightarrow \mathrm{T}_{\max }=σ_{\max }\times \mathrm{A}$

For the lower wire the area of cross-section is $\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{L}}=0.004\mathrm{cm}^{2}=4\times 10^{-7}\mathrm{m}^{2}$ :

$\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{L}(\max )}=\left (12\times 10^{8}\right )\times \left (4\times 10^{-7}\right )=480\mathrm{N}$

For the upper wire the area of cross-section is $A_{U}=0.008\mathrm{cm}^{2}=8\times 10^{-7}\mathrm{m}^{2}$ :

$\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{U}(\max )}=\left (12\times 10^{8}\right )\times \left (8\times 10^{-7}\right )=960\mathrm{N}$

Let M be the mass added to the pan.

As lower wire supports the pan and the 10 kg mass.


[IMG]


$T_{L}=(M+10)g=(M+10)\times 10$

For lower wire not to break:

$10(M+10)\leq 480\Rightarrow M+10\leq 48\Rightarrow M\leq 38\mathrm{kg}.....(ii)$

The upper wire supports the pan, 10 kg mass, and 30 kg mass.


[IMG]


$\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{U}}=(\mathrm{M}+10+30)\mathrm{g}=(\mathrm{M}+40)\times 10$

For upper wire not to break:

$10(M+40)\leq 960\Rightarrow M+40\leq 96\Rightarrow M\leq 56\mathrm{kg}\ldots (ii)$

To ensure neither wire breaks, we must choose the smaller of the two values. If we add 56 kg , the lower wire will break. If we add 38 kg , both wires remain intact. Therefore, the maximum load that can be placed in pan is 38 kg .

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 5th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The impedance of a series $RC$ circuit is given by $Z=\sqrt{R^{2}+X_{C}^{2}}$

If the voltage of a.c. source is V then the current in the circuit is $\mathrm{I}=\frac{\mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{Z}}$

The capacitive reactance at angular frequency $ω$ is $\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}}=\frac{1}{ω\mathrm{C}}$.

For current (I) when the frequency of the source is $ω$.

The capacitive reactance is $\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}}=\frac{1}{ω\mathrm{C}}$

$I=\frac{V}{\sqrt{R^{2}+X_{C}^{2}}}..(i)$

At frequency $ω^{'}=\frac{ω}{4}$, the new reactance $\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}}^{'}$ becomes $\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}}^{'}=\frac{1}{(ω/4)\mathrm{C}}=\frac{4}{ω\mathrm{C}}=4\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}}$

The new current $\mathrm{I}^{'}=\mathrm{I}/3$ :

$\frac{I}{3}=\frac{V}{\sqrt{R^{2}+(4X_{C})^{2}}}=\frac{V}{\sqrt{R^{2}+16X_{C}^{2}}}\ldots (ii)$

Substituting I from equation (i) into equation (ii) :

$\frac{1}{3}\left (\frac{V}{\sqrt{R^{2}+X_{C}^{2}}}\right )=\frac{V}{\sqrt{R^{2}+16X_{C}^{2}}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{9\left (R^{2}+X_{C}^{2}\right )}=\frac{1}{R^{2}+16X_{C}^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $R^{2}+16X_{C}^{2}=9R^{2}+9X_{C}^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $7X_{C}^{2}=8R^{2}$

So, the ratio of resistance to reactance $\left (\frac{\mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}}}\right )$

$\frac{\mathrm{R}^{2}}{\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}}^{2}}=\frac{7}{8}$

$\Rightarrow\frac{\mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}}}=\sqrt{\frac{7}{8}}$

Therefore, correct option is (C).

text: A cube has side length 5 cm and modulus of rigidity $10^{5}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}^{2}$. The displacement produced by a force of 10 N in the upper face of cube is $____$ mm.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 5th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The modulus of rigidity (or shear modulus) is defined as the ratio of shear stress to shear strain.

$η=\frac{\text{Shear Stress}}{\text{Shear Strain}}=\frac{\mathrm{F}/\mathrm{A}}{\Delta \mathrm{x}/\mathrm{L}}$


[IMG]


Where F is the tangential force applied, A is the area of the face, $\Delta \mathrm{x}$ is the relative displacement and L is the height (side length) of the cube.

The side length of cube is $\mathrm{L}=5\mathrm{cm}=0.05\mathrm{m}$

So, the area is $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{L}^{2}=(0.05)^{2}=0.0025\mathrm{m}^{2}=2.5\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{m}^{2}$

The magnitude of applied tangential force is $\mathrm{F}=10\mathrm{N}$

The shear modulus is $η=10^{5}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}^{2}$

Using the formula of shear modulus;

$η=\frac{\mathrm{FL}}{\mathrm{A}\Delta \mathrm{x}}\Rightarrow \Delta \mathrm{x}=\frac{\mathrm{FL}}{\mathrm{A}η}$

Putting the values,

$\Delta \mathrm{x}=\frac{10\times 0.05}{\left (2.5\times 10^{-3}\right )\times 10^{5}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta x=\frac{0.5}{2.5\times 10^{2}}=\frac{0.5}{250}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta \mathrm{x}=0.002\mathrm{m}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta \mathrm{x}=0.002\times 1000\mathrm{mm}=2\mathrm{mm}$

Therefore, the correct answer is 2 .

text:
From 18 m height above the ground a ball is dropped from rest . The height above the ground at which the magnitude of velocity equal to the magnitude of acceleration (in the same set of units) due to gravity is $____$ m.

solution.body:
It is given that the magnitude of velocity ( v ) must equal the magnitude of acceleration due to gravity ( g ).

$|\mathrm{v}|=\mathrm{g}$

As acceleration due to gravity is $\mathrm{g}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$; so, we need to find the point where $\mathrm{v}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$.

Using the third equation of motion:

$v^{2}=u^{2}+2gy$

Since the ball is dropped from rest, the initial velocity $u=0$.

Putting the values,

$(10)^{2}=0+2(10)y$

$\Rightarrow$ $100=20y$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{y}=5\mathrm{m}$

The ball has fallen 5 m from its starting point.

The total initial height $(\mathrm{H})$ is 18 m . The height above the ground is the total height minus the distance fallen:

$\mathrm{h}=\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{y}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{h}=18-5=13\mathrm{m}$

Therefore, at a height of 13 m the magnitude of velocity is same as acceleration due to gravity. 

Thus, the correct answer is 13 .

By comparing this with the given equation $\mathrm{y}=3\sin \left (36\mathrm{t}+0.018\mathrm{x}+\frac{π}{4}\right )$, the wave number is $\mathrm{k}=0.018\mathrm{cm}^{-1}$.

The wave number k is related to the wavelength by the formula:

$k=\frac{2π}{λ}$

Putting the value $\mathrm{k}=0.018$ and $π=3.14$ into the formula :

$0.018=\frac{2\times 3.14}{λ}$

$\Rightarrow$ $λ=\frac{6.28}{0.018}$

$\Rightarrow$ $λ\approx 349\mathrm{cm}$

Therefore, the wavelength of transverse wave is 349 cm . 

Thus, the correct answer is 349 .

text: The charged particle moving in a uniform magnetic field of $(3\hat{i}+2\hat{j})\mathrm{T}$ has an acceleration $\left (4\hat{i}-\frac{x}{2}\hat{j}\right )\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. The value of $x$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 5th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The force ( $⃗{F}$ ) acting on a particle with charge $q$ moving with velocity $⃗{v}$ in a magnetic field $⃗{B}$ is given by the Lorentz force law:

$\vec{\mathrm{F}}=\mathrm{q}(\vec{\mathrm{v}}\times \vec{\mathrm{B}})$

According to Newton's second law, $\vec{\mathrm{F}}=\mathrm{m}\vec{\mathrm{a}}$.

Therefore,

$\mathrm{m}\vec{\mathrm{a}}=\mathrm{q}(\vec{\mathrm{v}}\times \vec{\mathrm{B}})$

The resulting vector is always perpendicular to both $⃗{v}$ and $⃗{B}$.

Since $\vec{\mathrm{a}}$ is in the same direction as $\vec{\mathrm{F}}$, the acceleration vector $\vec{\mathrm{a}}$ must be perpendicular to the magnetic field vector $\vec{\mathrm{B}}$.

$\vec{\mathrm{a}}⟂\mathrm{B}\leftarrow$

If two vectors are perpendicular, their dot product must be zero:

$\vec{\mathrm{a}}\cdot \mathrm{B}\leftarrow =0$

The magnetic field is given as $⃗{B}=3\hat{ı}+2\hat{ȷ}$ and $⃗{a}=4\hat{ı}-\frac{x}{2}\hat{ȷ}$ :

$\left (4\hat{ı}-\frac{x}{2}\hat{ȷ}\right )\cdot (3\hat{ı}+2\hat{ȷ})=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $(4\times 3)+\left (-\frac{x}{2}\times 2\right )=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $12-x=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $x=12$

Therefore, the value of x is 12 .

text:
In the given circuit below inductance values of $L_{1},L_{2}$ and $L_{3}$ are same. The magnetic energy stored in the entire circuit is $(U_{t})$ and that stored in the $\mathrm{L}_{2}$ inductor is $(U_{l})$. $U_{t}/U_{l}$ is $____$ .

(Ignore the mutual inductance if any)

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 5th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The magnetic energy ( $U$ ) stored in an inductor of inductance $L$ carrying a current $I$ is given by the formula:

$\mathrm{U}=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{LI}^{2}$

In the given circuit $\mathrm{L}_{1}$ in series with a parallel combination of $\mathrm{L}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{L}_{3}$.

Let the total current entering the circuit be I.

Then the current through $\mathrm{L}_{1}$ is $\mathrm{I}_{1}=\mathrm{I}$.

Since $\mathrm{L}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{L}_{3}$ are in parallel and have the same inductance $(\mathrm{L}_{2}=\mathrm{L}_{3}=\mathrm{L})$, the current I will distribute equally between them.

So, the current through $\mathrm{L}_{2}$ is $\mathrm{I}_{2}=\frac{\mathrm{I}}{2}$ and current through $\mathrm{L}_{3}$ is $\mathrm{I}_{3}=\frac{\mathrm{I}}{2}$.

Using the energy formula for $L_{2}$ :

$\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{l}}=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{L}(\mathrm{I}_{2})^{2}=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{L}\left (\frac{\mathrm{I}}{2}\right )^{2}=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{L}\left (\frac{\mathrm{I}^{2}}{4}\right )=\frac{\mathrm{LI}^{2}}{8}$

The total energy is the sum of the energies stored in $\mathrm{L}_{1},\mathrm{L}_{2}$, and $\mathrm{L}_{3}$ :

$\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{t}}=\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{L}1}+\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{L}2}+\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{L}3}$

$\Rightarrow$ $U_{t}=\frac{1}{2}LI^{2}+\frac{1}{2}L\left (\frac{I}{2}\right )^{2}+\frac{1}{2}L\left (\frac{I}{2}\right )^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{t}}=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{LI}^{2}+\frac{1}{8}\mathrm{LI}^{2}+\frac{1}{8}\mathrm{LI}^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{t}}=\frac{4\mathrm{LI}^{2}+\mathrm{LI}^{2}+\mathrm{LI}^{2}}{8}=\frac{6\mathrm{LI}^{2}}{8}=\frac{3}{4}\mathrm{LI}^{2}$

So, the ratio of magnetic energy stored is $\frac{\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{t}}}{\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{l}}}$ is,

$\frac{\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{t}}}{\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{l}}}=\frac{\frac{3}{4}\mathrm{LI}^{2}}{\frac{1}{8}\mathrm{LI}^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{t}}}{\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{l}}}=\frac{3}{4}\times 8=3\times 2=6$

Therefore, the correct answer is 6 .
